acceptance.review: The installed boundary assertions cover 900000 ms, 900001 ms and seven days. Actual fresh Codex MCP reads of the original unmodified 6.3.1 proof at more than three hours old remain READY in 6.3.2 before and after restart. Profile, governed secret, binding and proof hashes remain unchanged; zero implicit preflight or binding writes were observed.

The unchanged aged governed GLM profile was selected by the ordinary Runtime Loop path and one actual external model request succeeded with 440 input and 1509 output tokens (1949 total), retaining its request receipt. Codex MCP readiness was independently read; the actual Loop start used the authenticated Runtime HTTP adapter. Neither a model-tool MCP execution nor a new preflight/rebind is claimed.

Installed named boundary and negative assertions retain initial/rebind freshness at 900000 ms, reject 900001 ms and malformed/future/missing proof, and preserve exact CAS, scope and governed SecretRef controls. The separate declared controlled-provider case exercised actual HTTP/RBAC/CAS refusals and explicit valid repairs through fresh Codex reads.

An isolated controlled provider returned an actual 503 and persisted failure evidence; subsequent genuine Codex MCP reads observed refusal. Profile drift and SecretRef revocation also refused operation, with final revocation intentionally remaining blocked. Named current tests cover proof/model/baseUrl/reference/status/scope drift. This was not a fabricated external GLM outage and daily provider inputs were unchanged.

The aged-profile and restart observations record zero implicit preflight and binding writes, with one and only one explicit external model start. Twenty-one controlled-case MCP reads were checked against four explicit provider requests. Current inherited named and case evidence retains request scope, unknown-outcome non-replay, token/time limits and the absence of a product currency setting. The retained restart receipt was resumed without redispatching its successful model request.

An isolated exact install used retained real 6.3.1 persisted bindings and private inputs, with no credential entry or timestamp edits. Candidate initial and restart phases both returned READY through fresh Codex MCP contexts; original snapshot/private configuration and daily Runtime files were unchanged. The qualified product paths used current Expert, Harness and independent extensions, with no retired Suite fallback.

All 409 immutable published 6.3.1 definitions and 1303 sub-obligations have current item-specific impact dispositions, bound to 628 named assertions, 704 source inputs and four cases. Exact installed regression passed 2414 of 2414 tests with no skipped/failing tests and no build, source or library mutation. Expert 2.3.0, Harness 4.8.1 and extensions 1.0.1 complete executable inventories match retained inputs. Historical journey PASS was not transferred; one-time migration/deletion was not repeated.

The sole accepted Candidate is source 05da3339b32468f3682eea8a1c2b31880a6c38a1 from successful workflow 37177531263 attempt 1. Its 16 release assets, exact handoff, release set, approved Target and installed libraries are pinned and verified; no Runtime rebuild occurred during installation or regression. The source maintenance request completed through the scoped qualified Codex path with retained original receipt. Actual installed cases and full Candidate checks supplement the artifact identity evidence.

Four newly executed isolated phases verify candidate initial install, restart, rollback to 6.3.1 and reapply to 6.3.2. The 6.3.1 rollback correctly exposes its known age-based block; 6.3.2 initial/restart/reapply are READY. Original private inputs, persisted Loop/model metrics, daily data and independent identities are unchanged. Restart comparison recovery permits only the source-defined live watchdog age field and never repeats the completed model call. Current daily installation remains a separate post-publication transaction.

Seven exact Candidate source documents describe initial proof freshness, durable unchanged binding, real failure/drift refusal, explicit repair, no implicit probe and the v1 expiresAt meaning. The installed protocol unit assertion verifies Runtime 6.3.2. Public pointers correctly remain on the observed 6.3.1 release until 6.3.2 is actually published, when a separate guarded projection will update them. Native credential interaction and a new 90-minute soak are excluded and never counted as PASS.
